title: Pharmacological NOX2 inhibition reduces endothelial inflammatory activation in experimental atherosclerosis
abstract: In a mouse model of diet-induced atherosclerosis, pharmacological inhibition of NOX2 reduced vascular reactive oxygen species, decreased VCAM-1 expression, and reduced monocyte adhesion to the endothelium. Lesion area was modestly decreased compared with vehicle-treated controls.

title: Complete Nox2 deficiency accelerates lesion formation in hyperlipidaemic mice
abstract: Nox2 knockout mice crossed onto a hyperlipidaemic background developed larger atherosclerotic lesions than control animals. The authors reported impaired vascular homeostasis and increased inflammatory cell accumulation despite reduced canonical NOX2-derived oxidant production.

title: NOX2 inhibition has stage-dependent effects on plaque inflammation and repair
abstract: NOX2 inhibition reduced early endothelial activation and inflammatory cytokine expression. However, late treatment did not reduce plaque size and was associated with impaired endothelial repair markers. The findings suggest that the effect of NOX2 inhibition depends on disease stage and endpoint measured.

title: NOX2 expression is associated with oxidative stress in human atherosclerotic plaques
abstract: Human plaque samples showed increased NOX2 expression in regions with high oxidative stress and macrophage accumulation. The study was observational and did not directly test whether NOX2 inhibition reduces atherosclerosis.

title: Endothelial CYBB knockdown suppresses adhesion molecule expression after inflammatory stimulation
abstract: In cultured endothelial cells, CYBB knockdown reduced inflammatory-stimulus-induced VCAM-1 and ICAM-1 expression. Monocyte adhesion was reduced, but the study did not measure plaque formation or atherosclerotic lesion size.

title: NADPH oxidase signalling supports vascular repair after endothelial injury
abstract: In an endothelial injury model, broad suppression of NADPH oxidase signalling impaired endothelial repair and delayed restoration of barrier integrity. The study suggests that complete suppression of oxidase signalling may have harmful vascular effects in some contexts.

title: NOX2 and inflammatory signalling in vascular disease: a review
abstract: This review summarises evidence linking NOX2-derived reactive oxygen species to vascular inflammation, endothelial activation, macrophage function, and plaque progression. It discusses both protective and harmful effects reported across experimental models but does not present new primary data.

title: Low-dose NOX2 inhibition reduces monocyte recruitment without altering plaque size
abstract: Low-dose NOX2 inhibition reduced circulating inflammatory markers and decreased monocyte recruitment into vascular lesions. However, total plaque area was unchanged after treatment. The authors concluded that inflammatory endpoints improved without clear structural benefit.
